title: Chapter IX · How carefully the soul must bear itself after the visitation of grace

blocks.s: 10. But take care, O bride: when the Bridegroom absents himself, he will not go far; and though you do not see him, he always sees you, full of eyes before and behind. You can never be hidden from him. He also has his messengers about you, spirits like the most sagacious of scouts, to see how you behave while the Bridegroom is away, and to accuse you before him if they catch in you any signs of wantonness or buffoonery. This Bridegroom is jealous. If perhaps you receive another lover, if you strive to please others more, he will at once leave you and cling to other maidens. This Bridegroom is delicate; he is noble and rich, beautiful in form above the sons of men; and so he deigns to have none but a beautiful bride. If he sees a stain or a wrinkle in you, he at once turns his eyes away. He can bear no uncleanness. Be chaste, then; be modest and humble, so that you may deserve to be visited often by your Bridegroom. I fear this talk has held us too long; but a subject at once fertile and sweet drove me to it, and I did not draw it out of my own will, but was drawn on unwilling by some sweetness of it, I know not what.
